newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Stg strength to hold back Burmah.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Stg strength to hold back Burmah.

text.p: Lubricants producer Burmah Castrol Plc is set to report only a mild increase in its 1996 profits on Monday despite a strong underlying business performance.
Analysts said the strength of the pound versus the dollar, the rupee and several European currencies will have severely restricted the overall profit rise.
They predict net income before exceptional items in a tight range of 139.5 to 141.5 million stg compared with 135.0 million stg the previous year.
Without the negative pound impact, profits would likely have risen to around 150 million stg, analayst said.
Adverse currency translation effects will make themselves felt again this year, when profit is forecast somewhere near 145 million.
February's release of Castrol India's results underlined just how currency sensitive Burmah Castrol's results are.
Castrol India, which is 51 percent owned by Burmah Castrol, saw full-year profits climb 19 percent in rupee terms, but showed a rise of only nine percent when calculated in pounds.
Castrol India is Burmah's third biggest profit centre.
"You can see that the underlying business is doing extremely well, but that on translation the growth appears only mediocre," said analyst Irene Himona at SocGen.
The growth of Burmah Castrol's operations is mainly fuelled by its lubricants business, which builds on the worldwide strength of its Castrol brand name.
"They have a phenomenal global postion in branded lubricants," said another analyst.
Burmah's specialist chemicals business will also have contributed, but that would mainly be the result of a lengthy restructuring process.

Burmah indicated last year that the reorgainsation is now completed, opening the way for expansion in growth areas such as Asia. The company is expected to help boost its presence there through several small acquisitions over the next couple of years.
